title: The Quran's First Prayer Is Answered by Its First Sentence

substrate_check.1:6: ٱهْدِ = V | IMPV | VF:1 | ROOT:هدي | 2MS, followed by نَا (PRON|SUFF|1P) => 'guide us', imperative plea. CONFIRMED.
substrate_check.1:7: continuation of the sirat description (ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ...); NOTE 1:7, not 1:6, is al-Fatiha's literal last ayah. ihdina is the closing REQUEST verb; the du'a unit is 1:6-7.
substrate_check.2:1: single INL muqatta'at segment الٓمٓ. CONFIRMED (so 2:2 is the first CONTENT sentence).
substrate_check.2:2: هُدًى = N | ROOT:هدي | INDEF | NOM, opened by demonstrative ذَٰلِكَ (DEM). Same root هدي as 1:6. CONFIRMED.
substrate_check.seam: mushaf order places last content-verse of surah 1 immediately before first content-verse of surah 2. Root-echo هدي across the seam is a real lexical fact, mechanically verified in scripts/.corpus-cache/quranic-corpus.json.
substrate_check.verdict: Substrate CONFIRMED. Root echo is real, not projected.

imposed_test: PASS. The request->answer reading at this seam is NOT a modern imposition: it is a canonical inter-surah munasaba (tanasub al-suwar). al-Tabari and al-Jalalayn both gloss ذَٰلِكَ as presentational هذا ('THIS Book'), supporting the 'here it is' answer-shape. al-Fatiha-as-du'a is Ibn al-Qayyim's central thesis in Madarij al-Salikin (the book is built around iyyaka na'budu wa iyyaka nasta'in). Reveal survives the real-vs-imposed test.
disguised_count_test: PASS. Not a frequency claim. It is a positional/lexical adjacency claim (root هدي on both sides of the 1/2 seam) plus a request->answer shape. Does not reduce to 'this word appears N times.'
overlap_test: CLEAN on content. published-articles.md: zero hits (fatiha/ihdina/hudan/2:2/munasaba/seam). Kahf 18:1-5 file cites 2:2 only as a general 'trustworthy Book' parallel (line 228), never linking it to ihdina. Fatiha 006-007 file frames 1:6 as 'the first du'a' and says 'the guidance is coming' (line 246) but NEVER names 2:2 as the answer. SOFT NOTE: the seam-munasaba LENS is already used on-site (Isra 17:111 -> Kahf 18:1, 'the two surahs meet at the mouth', Kahf file lines 200/298); and the du'a framing of 1:6 is already in the Fatiha 006-007 file. Content is distinct; the lens/framing is not novel to the site.
quran_only_test: PASS. Reveal is Quran->Quran (1:6 -> 2:2). No hadith payoff required. (Ibn al-Qayyim's du'a framing partly leans on the hadith qudsi 'qasamtu al-salata', but the article's core reveal stands on the text alone.)
hostile_tweet: 'AyahGuide says al-Razi and Ibn al-Qayyim state OUTRIGHT that Baqarah 2:2 answers al-Fatiha's ihdina. But the crisp "here is the Guidance you begged from Me" line is Mawdudi's (d. 1979) — modern. Show me the page in Mafatih al-Ghayb / Madarij where the classical imams say it. Name-dropping classical authorities for a modern framing is the credibility problem.' -- This tweet LANDS unless the two pinned classical citations are verified in primary text. It is the load-bearing vulnerability of the FRAMING (not of the reveal).
broken_claims: 'unimpeachably classical' + 'al-Razi opens his al-Baqarah commentary on the sequence' + 'Ibn al-Qayyim states it outright': the two PINNED classical attributions are UNVERIFIED. My tafsir tool (Ibn Kathir/al-Tabari/al-Muyassar/al-Jalalayn) cannot reach al-Razi or Ibn al-Qayyim, and web search did not confirm either specific claim. Worse, the crispest form of this exact reading -- al-Fatiha is the prayer, the Quran/2:2 is the answer, 'This is the Guidance you begged from Me' -- is most prominently attributed to MAWDUDI (Tafhim al-Qur'an, 20th c.), a MODERN mufassir. The general munasaba is old; the specific 'the classical imams state 2:2 = the answer outright' confidence is overstated and possibly misattributed.

'answers word-for-word': false as literally stated. 1:6 ٱهْدِ is an imperative VERB; 2:2 هُدًى is a NOUN. They share the ROOT هدي, not the word. (Exhibit ground_notes already self-flagged this; the fix must actually be applied.)
Framing that treats 1:6 (ihdina) as al-Fatiha's closing ayah: 1:7 is the literal last verse. ihdina is the closing REQUEST verb; phrase as 'al-Fatiha's closing request (1:6-7)'.
required_corrections: 1) DE-PIN THE CLASSICAL ATTRIBUTIONS. Before any 'classical/unimpeachably classical' claim, verify in PRIMARY ARABIC that (a) al-Razi's Mafatih al-Ghayb intro to al-Baqarah actually opens on the ihdina->hudan sequence, and (b) Ibn al-Qayyim in Madarij al-Salikin actually states 2:2 is God's answer to ihdina. If either cannot be pinned to a specific passage, DROP the pinned citation and reframe to: 'a celebrated munasaba (tanasub al-suwar) -- rooted in the classical framing of al-Fatiha as du'a (Ibn al-Qayyim, Madarij) and the sirat as the Book, and stated crisply by later mufassirun including Mawdudi (Tafhim al-Qur'an).' False classical attribution is a worse landmine than an honest 'old idea, sharpest modern wording' frame. 2) Apply the exhibit's own fix: 'same root (هدي)', NOT 'word-for-word' -- 1:6 is a verb, 2:2 a noun. 3) Keep the basmala-numbering caution (Hafs counts basmala as 1:1): say 'closing request / first content-sentence', never 'last ayah / verse 1'. 4) Phrase ihdina as the closing REQUEST (du'a unit 1:6-7); 1:7 is the literal last verse. 5) Heed the proposal's own risk: keep the safe claim ('the seam reads as request-and-answer'); do NOT inflate to an unattributed global 'the whole Quran is compositionally structured as an answered du'a.' 6) EDITORIAL: build on / link the existing Fatiha 006-007 tadabbur file (which already frames 1:6 as 'the first du'a') rather than re-presenting that framing as new; and since the site already uses the seam-munasaba lens (Isra->Kahf), scope 'rare structural reveal' to the CONTENT, not the method.
notes: The REVEAL survives every core test: substrate is mechanically CONFIRMED (root هدي at the 1/2 seam, imperative ٱهْدِ + 1P vs noun هُدًى, demonstrator ذَٰلِكَ read presentationally by al-Tabari/al-Jalalayn); it is a REAL canonical munasaba, not an imposed modern reading; not a disguised count; overlap clean on content; Quran-only payoff. The one load-bearing failure is on the DISTINCTIVE FRAMING, not the content: the proposal's selling point ('unimpeachably classical', with al-Razi 'opening on this' and Ibn al-Qayyim 'stating it outright') is UNVERIFIED and the crispest attested wording of this exact reading is MODERN (Mawdudi). That is correctable without killing the piece -- so SURVIVES, conditional on the attribution being verified in primary text or downgraded. Publishable as a strong munasaba reflection; NOT publishable with pinned classical citations a reader could check and find absent.
